title: Mortgage foreclosure and loss-mitigation protections
facts: Federal mortgage-servicing rules provide loss-mitigation procedures for many borrowers with covered mortgage loans.
A servicer generally may not make the first notice or filing required for foreclosure until the loan is more than 120 days delinquent, subject to specified exceptions.
Submitting a complete loss-mitigation application can trigger evaluation and procedural protections under federal rules depending on timing.
Foreclosure also depends heavily on state law, so federal servicing rules do not replace state foreclosure procedures.
